name: Ch’ēng-kung Sui
bio: Ch’ēng-kung Sui died in AD 273. He is represented here by a single short poem, “Inviting Guests,” which describes a gathering of friends for talk and plain food.
The poems here are Arthur Waley’s version in A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems (1918), given with the poet’s name as spelled in those books.

poems.title: Inviting Guests
poems.author: Ch’ēng-kung Sui
poems.collection: A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems (1918)
poems.text:
I sent out invitations
To summon guests.
I collected together
All my friends.
Loud talk
And simple feasting:
Discussion of philosophy,
Investigation of subtleties.
Tongues loosened
And minds at one.
Hearts refreshed
By discharge of emotion!
